newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union confident over Lufthansa strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Union confident over Lufthansa strike vote.

text.p: Germany's DAG trade union said on Wednesday it was confident that enough of its members would vote in favour of strikes in its pay dispute with Deutsche Lufthansa for strikes to go ahead.
"The incoming voting documents that we have received so show us that we shall reach the quorum of 70 percent," DAG chief negotiator Michael Tarp said by telephone.

Tarp said Lufthansa's earlier announcement of plans to streamline its management and administration staff with a minimum 10 percent would be seen as a "declaration of war" by some of the airline's 50,000-plus staff.

He said that the union feared the internal organisation would allow Lufthansa in a few years' time to spin out its operations into legally-separate operating divisions, thus allowing it to renegotiate cheaper worker contracts.
"In that sense it looks as if our worst expectations could be exceeded," he said. The ballot is due to end on February 25.
Tarp said the move would clearly influence its members in favour of striking, adding that the union was already confident of strong support for strikes among cockpit and groundstaff.
"We still have some to do with cabin staff, but we think that there too we shall reach the 70 percent," he said.

DAG has rejected all wage offers presented to it by Lufthansa so far as insufficient. It has already led two limited industrial stoppages at the airline which have cost Lufthansa tens of millions of marks.
